The five towers in the middle of Angkor Wat represent **Mount Meru**. In Hinduism and Buddhism it is regarded as the centre of the world and the home of the gods. The broad **moat** around the complex stands for the ocean that surrounds the world. In the galleries, a relief about 50 metres long shows the **churning of the Ocean of Milk**. Gods and demons pull on a giant snake in order to win a drink of immortality.

The small temple of **Banteay Srei** was consecrated in the year 967. It is built of **pink sandstone** and is famous for its especially fine reliefs. It was founded not by a king but by a high **Brahmin**, that is, a priest. Its name means roughly “Citadel of the Women”.

In the years 1296 to 1297, the Chinese envoy **Zhou Daguan** lived in Angkor. He came on behalf of the Yuan dynasty. His report is the only surviving **eyewitness account** of everyday life. It describes markets, festivals, clothing and the king of the Khmer.

King **Jayavarman VII** ruled around the year 1200 and was a Buddhist. Inscriptions report that he had **102 hospitals** with staff and medicines built throughout the kingdom. In addition there were rest houses along the roads. In 1992, Angkor was added to the **UNESCO World Heritage List** and at the same time classed as endangered. Thanks to restoration work it was removed from that list again in 2004.

gewusst: Angkor was among the biggest cities in the world before industrialisation.
For centuries, many temples were overgrown by the jungle.

teile.einleitung: The Phoenicians were a people of seafarers and traders on the eastern Mediterranean. They developed a script with only a few signs, each standing for one sound. From it arose many alphabets of today, including ours.
wichtigste: The Phoenician alphabet had only 22 letters.
Each sign stood for a sound, not for a whole word.
The vowels had no signs of their own.
The Phoenicians wrote from right to left.
The Greeks took over the alphabet and developed it further.
From the sign for ox came our A, from the sign Beth for house our B.
The word “Bible” goes back indirectly to the Phoenician city of Byblos.

abschnitte.text: The **Phoenicians** lived on the coast of present-day **Lebanon**. Their most important cities were **Byblos**, Tyre and Sidon. With their ships they sailed all over the Mediterranean and founded trading cities such as Carthage. For their business they needed a script that could be learned and written quickly. About 3,000 years ago their alphabet was fully developed.

Other scripts such as the Egyptian hieroglyphs had hundreds of signs. The Phoenicians managed with **22 letters**. Each sign stood for **one sound**. That was a great relief, because now many more people could learn to read and write. However, there were only signs for consonants, and the **vowels** such as a, e or o were missing. The reader had to supply them while reading.

The Phoenicians wrote **from right to left**. That is how Hebrew and Arabic are still written today. These two scripts also descend, by roundabout routes, from the Phoenician script. The oldest inscriptions are found on stones, for example on a royal sarcophagus in Byblos.

The **Greeks** came to know the Phoenician script through trade. They took over the signs and added signs of their own for the **vowels**. In time they wrote from left to right. From the Greek alphabet later arose the **Latin alphabet** of the Romans. That is the script we write with today.

Many letters have a long history. The Phoenician sign **aleph** meant **ox** and looked like an ox's head. From it came our **A**. The sign **beth** meant **house** and became our **B**. The Greeks called the two letters **alpha and beta**, and from them came the word **alphabet**. And because the Greeks obtained papyrus via **Byblos**, they called the book “biblion”. From that comes the word **Bible**.

gewusst: If you turn a capital A upside down, you can still recognise the horns of an ox.
Almost all alphabets of the world go back to the script of the Phoenicians.

teile.einleitung: The first Greek philosophers are called the Pre-Socratics. They lived before or at the time of Socrates. They were the first to ask what the world is made of, and looked for answers in nature instead of only in legends about gods.
wichtigste: The Pre-Socratics are the earliest Greek philosophers.
Many came from cities in **Asia Minor**, today's western Turkey.
**Thales** held water to be the primal source of all things.
**Anaximander** spoke of the **apeiron**, the unlimited.
**Anaximenes** regarded air as the primal substance.
**Heraclitus** of Ephesus saw fire as the basic principle.
**Democritus** and Leucippus taught that everything is made of atoms.

abschnitte.titel: What is the world made of?
abschnitte.text: The Pre-Socratics searched for the **primal source** of all things, in Greek **arche**. They wanted to know what substance everything had arisen from. In doing so they tried to explain the world with **reason**. Only fragments of their books survive, so-called **fragments**. We know much of it only from accounts by later writers.

The first philosopher is considered to be **Thales of Miletus**. He held **water** to be the primal source of all things. According to the historian Herodotus, he is said to have predicted a **solar eclipse**. His pupil **Anaximander** thought of an unlimited primal substance, the **apeiron**. **Anaximenes**, also from Miletus, saw **air** as the primal substance.

**Heraclitus** came from **Ephesus** in Asia Minor. For him, **fire** was the basic principle of the world. He believed that everything was constantly changing. The saying is attributed to him: “You cannot step into the same river twice.” For when you step in for the second time, other water is already there.

**Leucippus** and his pupil **Democritus** developed an astonishing idea. They believed that everything consists of tiny **indivisible particles**. They called these **atoms**, after the Greek word for “indivisible”. Between the atoms there was empty space. Only much later could natural science show that atoms really exist.

The Pre-Socratics asked questions that still occupy people today. Their way of thinking was a beginning of **philosophy** and **natural science**. Later philosophers such as Plato and Aristotle dealt in detail with their ideas. Pythagoras, Parmenides and Empedocles are also counted among the Pre-Socratics.

gewusst: Today's atoms can in fact be divided, but their name still recalls Democritus's idea.
Empedocles taught that everything consists of four elements: earth, water, air and fire. This idea lasted for almost two thousand years.

teile.einleitung: Oracle bones are bones and tortoise shells with which the kings of the Shang Dynasty in ancient China consulted the future. The inscriptions scratched into them are the oldest substantial evidence of Chinese writing.
wichtigste: Oracle bones come from the time of the Shang Dynasty in China.
Mainly ox shoulder blades and tortoise shells were used.
The bone was heated and the cracks were interpreted.
Question and result were scratched into the bone.
The scholar Wang Yirong recognised the signs as writing in 1899.
Many signs can be linked with present-day Chinese characters.

abschnitte.text: The **Shang Dynasty** ruled in the 2nd millennium BC in the north of China. Before important decisions its kings wanted to know what the **ancestors** and gods thought of them. For this they used **oracle bones**. Mainly **ox shoulder blades** and the **underside shells of tortoises** were used. These flat pieces could be worked and inscribed easily.

In the bones small **hollows** were first drilled or cut. Then **heat** was applied there until **cracks** appeared in the bone. From the shape of the cracks the answer of the ancestors was read. Afterwards the **question** and often also the **result** were scratched into the bone. People asked, for example, about the weather, the harvest, hunts, wars or illnesses.

For a long time nobody knew what these bones were. Farmers found them in the ground, and **pharmacies** sold them ground up as **“dragon bones”** for medicine. In **1899** the scholar **Wang Yirong** recognised that the scratched signs are a very old **script**. After that researchers searched specifically for sites. Most of the bones were found near **Anyang**, where a capital of the Shang lay.

The inscriptions from the late Shang period are the **earliest larger amounts of text** in Chinese script. Many signs still look like small pictures, for example for person, sun or horse. Even so, many can be linked with **present-day characters**. So Chinese writing has been used without a break for over 3,000 years. The bones also reveal a lot about life at the royal court.

gewusst: The oracle bones were first sold as “dragon bones” in pharmacies.
Chinese writing is one of the oldest scripts still in use today.

teile.einleitung: Ur was one of the most important cities of the Sumerians in Mesopotamia. Its ruins lie today in the south of Iraq. Ur became famous through rich royal tombs full of treasures.
wichtigste: The ruins of Ur lie in present-day **Iraq**.
In ancient times the city lay on the **Euphrates**.
The British researcher **Leonard Woolley** excavated Ur around 100 years ago.
In the royal tombs, **gold jewellery** was found.
The richest tomb belonged to a queen named **Puabi**.
Famous finds are the **Standard of Ur**, lyres and a board game.

abschnitte.text: Ur lay in the south of **Mesopotamia**, the land between the Euphrates and the Tigris. In ancient times the **Euphrates** flowed right past the city. Today the river has changed its course and lies further away. Ur was an important city of the **Sumerians** with temples, palaces and a harbour. Above the city rose a stepped temple tower, the **ziggurat**.

In the 1920s and 1930s, the British archaeologist **Leonard Woolley** excavated Ur. He and his team worked for many years. In doing so they discovered a large cemetery with **royal tombs**. Many finds went to the museums in London, Philadelphia and Baghdad.

The tomb of Queen **Puabi** was especially rich. There they found **gold jewellery** and coloured gemstones, vessels and a magnificent headdress. Her name was on a small seal. Grave goods like these show how rich and skilful the craftsmen of Ur were.

In the tombs there were also **lyres**, string instruments made of wood, decorated with gold and a bull's head. A **board game** was also found, which is now called the “Royal Game of Ur”. A famous box is the **Standard of Ur**. On one side it shows pictures of war, and on the other a feast in peacetime.

The Bible says that **Abraham** came from “Ur of the Chaldeans”. Many researchers link this place with the Ur of the Sumerians. But this cannot be proved for certain. Today the ruins of Ur are a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

gewusst: Researchers were able to work out the rules of the Royal Game of Ur in part thanks to a much later cuneiform tablet. Today some people play it again.
The lyres of Ur are among the oldest surviving string instruments in the world.

teile.einleitung: The Minoan civilisation was the first advanced civilisation of Europe. It flourished in the Bronze Age on the island of Crete, with magnificent palaces, colourful wall paintings and a script that nobody understands to this day.
wichtigste: The Minoan civilisation flourished in the Bronze Age on Crete.
Arthur Evans named it after the legendary King Minos.
Knossos was its largest centre, with over a thousand rooms.
The Minoans wrote in Linear A, a script that has not been deciphered.
Their palaces already had water pipes and drains.
The volcanic eruption on Thera (Santorini) also hit the Minoan world hard.

abschnitte.text: The Minoans lived in the **Bronze Age** on **Crete**, above all in the 2nd millennium BC. Their largest centre was **Knossos** near present-day **Heraklion**. The palace had over a thousand rooms, courts, stairways and storerooms. Further palaces stood at **Phaistos**, Malia and Zakros. The palaces had astonishing technology: clay pipes for **water supply** and channels for **sewage**.

What the Minoans called themselves is unknown. The English archaeologist **Arthur Evans**, who dug at Knossos from 1900, coined the term “Minoan” after the mythical King **Minos**. According to the legend Minos ruled in Knossos and kept the **Minotaur** captive in the **Labyrinth**, a creature half man, half bull. Many link the winding palace with this labyrinth.

The Minoans were seafarers and traders. Greek writers reported later that King Minos ruled the **Aegean** with his fleet. Such rule over the sea is called a **thalassocracy**, for “thalassa” is the Greek word for sea. Minoan goods and influences were found in Egypt, on many islands and on the Greek mainland.

The Minoans wrote, among other things, in **Linear A**, a syllabic script, mainly on clay tablets. Many signs can be read roughly phonetically thanks to the later script Linear B. But the language behind it is still not understood. Even more mysterious is the **Phaistos Disc**: the clay disc was found in **1908**. Its signs were pressed in with stamps and run in a spiral towards the centre. They have not been interpreted.

In the 2nd millennium BC the volcano on the island of **Thera**, today **Santorini**, erupted violently. Santorini lies only about 110 kilometres north of Crete. Ash and tidal waves devastated the Aegean and also harmed Crete. Whether the eruption directly caused the **decline** of the Minoans is **disputed** in research. Later Mycenaeans from the Greek mainland took over rule in Knossos.

gewusst: The signs on the Phaistos Disc were stamped, a very early kind of printing.
Wall paintings from Knossos show young people leaping over bulls.

teile.einleitung: The Ptolemaic Kingdom was a Greek-ruled kingdom in Egypt. It arose after the death of Alexander the Great and lasted about 300 years. Its capital Alexandria became a centre of learning.
wichtigste: Its founder was Ptolemy I, with the epithet Soter, that is, Saviour.
The capital was Alexandria with its famous library.
The Ptolemies promoted the god Serapis for Greeks and Egyptians alike.
The scholar Eratosthenes calculated the circumference of the Earth in Alexandria with astonishing accuracy.
In Alexandria the Septuagint came into being, a Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible.
Against the Seleucid Empire the Ptolemies fought the Syrian Wars.
The last ruler was Cleopatra VII, after which Egypt became Roman.

abschnitte.text: After the death of **Alexander the Great** in 323 BC his generals divided the huge empire among themselves. The general **Ptolemy** took over Egypt. Later he made himself king. He received the epithet **Soter**, which means **Saviour**. All his successors were likewise called Ptolemy, which is why people speak of the **Ptolemaic Kingdom**.

The capital **Alexandria** lay on the Mediterranean coast. There the Ptolemies had the famous **library** and the Museion built, a research centre for scholars. The scholar **Eratosthenes** calculated the **circumference of the Earth** in the 3rd century BC with astonishing accuracy. To do so he compared the shadow of the sun at two different places. Outside the city stood the **Lighthouse of Pharos**, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

The rulers were Greeks, but most of the inhabitants were Egyptians. The Ptolemies had themselves portrayed like pharaohs and built Egyptian temples. They promoted the god **Serapis**, who combined features of Greek and Egyptian gods. Many Jews also lived in Alexandria. For them the **Septuagint** came into being, a translation of the Hebrew Bible into Greek.

With the neighbouring **Seleucid Empire** the Ptolemies disputed territories in present-day Syria and Israel for a long time. These struggles are called the **Syrian Wars**. Within the ruling family there were special customs. For example **Ptolemy II** married his sister **Arsinoe II**, following the model of old Egyptian royal houses. Later this happened more often among the Ptolemies.

The last and best known ruler was **Cleopatra VII**. She allied herself with the Romans Caesar and Mark Antony. After the defeat in the naval battle of Actium she died in **30 BC**. After that Egypt became a Roman province. With that the Ptolemaic Kingdom ended.

gewusst: The famous Rosetta Stone, with a text in three scripts, dates from the time of the Ptolemies.
Cleopatra VII is said to have been one of the few Ptolemaic rulers who also spoke the Egyptian language.
